title: Strings in Depth
summary: How Rust strings really work - UTF-8 bytes, chars and why there is no indexing by position, char_indices and safe slicing, building strings with push, push_str, + and format!, splitting, trimming and searching, case conversion, parsing, and converting between String, &str, char and bytes.

cards.a:
`len` counts bytes, and `é` takes two bytes in UTF-8

A `String` is UTF-8: ASCII takes one byte, `é` two, and others up to four. `s.chars().count()` counts characters.

cards.q: How do you get each character together with the byte position where it starts?
cards.a:
`s.char_indices()`

`char_indices()` gives (byte position, char) pairs. `chars().enumerate()` counts characters, so its numbers are wrong for slicing once a multi-byte character appears.

cards.q: Which is a valid way to get the first character of a `String` `s`?
cards.a:
`s.chars().next()`

Strings are not indexable by position; `chars()` goes through the characters, and `next()` gives the first (an `Option<char>`).
